feedback: Written before this geometry has raced. Evidence from iteration 1: all 60 trials lost the line once and then left the track at max_error 0.061 to 0.065, with steering_oscillation at 0.067 to 0.159. The line-loss distance matches the outer sensor's coverage edge, so the span is the first suspect. What I had to do: I kept the iteration 1 controller (kp 2.5, kd 0.15, base_speed 1.6, last_direction) and the [-2,-1,0,1,2] weights, because the signal is in weight units and does not change scale with span. The outer sensors now reach the signal limit at a larger lateral error, which raises gain at the edges. Next race, if line_loss_events fall and max_error stays under 0.06 on bends, keep the span and try wheel_track 0.12 m to add turn stability. If line_loss_events do not fall, the limit is turn authority, not sensing, so move wheel_track or wheel_radius next. If slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2, reduce kp before changing geometry.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events fall but max_error still reaches about 0.06 on bends, set wheel_track to 0.12 m with the ±0.06 span kept, because iteration 1 showed max_error at the 0.06 floor and a wider track gives more turn stability.
If line_loss_events do not fall after the span change, try wheel_radius 0.035 (or wheel_track 0.12) to raise turn authority, since iteration 1 lost the line at the same distance with the ±0.04 span.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 on slalom with the wider span, move the sensor row to y = 0.02 with the 16 mm footprint, because the closer row was tested in iteration 1 only at y = 0.03 and the oscillation was already near 0.16 there.
